title: Generative AI in Industrial and Manufacturing Contexts: A Systematic Review of Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
content: This systematic review examines the development, application domains, and implementation challenges of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) in industrial and manufacturing contexts. Based on 373 academic sources published between 2022 and 2026 and retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, and the ACM Digital Library, the study combines PRISMA-guided screening, bibliometric analysis, keyword normalization, co-occurrence mapping, and thematic synthesis. The findings reveal two dominant research trajectories. The first is an engineering-generation trajectory focused on generative design, topology optimization, additive manufacturing, lattice and metamaterial structures, and materials discovery. The second is a knowledge-intensive industrial-intelligence trajectory centered on large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, electronic design automation, semiconductor and circuit design, smart-manufacturing support, robotics-enabled industrial assistance, and human–AI co-design. Across these domains, GAI supports design-space exploration, manufacturability-aware optimization, synthetic-data generation, engineering-knowledge reuse, product customization, and workflow-level decision support. However, industrial deployment remains constrained by data quality, validation, explainability, intellectual property protection, cybersecurity, computational cost, enterprise-system integration, and the need for human oversight. The review maps the field’s thematic structure and identifies key barriers and opportunities for developing trustworthy, interoperable, and workflow-integrated industrial GAI systems.
